rv.q: It is well worth your time to see Wells And Welles and experience this world premiere production.
Crider convincingly creates conversation that is thought-provoking and pithy without sounding preachy or epigrammatic.

It is a compact and unique study of two men who are as famous even decades later, a clash between a brash young American and an aging Brit, and a thoughtful reflection on the nature of art and storytelling.
This delightful world premiere production tells the story of one day in the life of these two world-renowned figures.
"Wells and Welles" isn't a perfect show, but there's something magical about the way it brings the past to life.
The exceptionally well written dialogue by Chicago playwright Amy Crider is superbly performed by Blatchford and Wilford.
In sum, “Wells and Welles” is a cleverly constructed and well-written show that is not only a credit to Crider’s insightful vision but also a noteworthy personal achievement.

cn.t: Critics praise this compelling world premiere about the 1940 meeting between H.G. Wells and Orson Welles, calling it a smart "war of words" between two great minds clashing over "War of the Worlds."
